newsitem.title: USA: No one questioned EMU timetable at G7 -- Trichet.
newsitem.headline: No one questioned EMU timetable at G7 -- Trichet.

text.p: None of the ministers and central bank heads at Group of Seven talks on Sunday questioned whether European monetary union would be launched on time in January 1999, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said.
"The euro is there. No one questioned the timetable for a second," he told a news conference.

He also said the G7 had very briefly raised the question of how the European Union would deal with the risk of currency speculation between the decision due in May 1998 on which countries qualify to join and the launch of the euro in 1999.
"It was a point which was very, very briefly raised, to say that we would find the means to avoid this completely," he said.

He and French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis both declined to say what these means would be, though economists believe EU leaders will announce early -- possibly in May 1998 -- how they plan to fix exchange rates between currencies joining the euro.
Arthuis also said that the United States had expressed no worries about the risk of a delay to monetary union.
"I did not sense any uncertainty from them," he said.
"The euro is recognised today. The timetable for the euro will be respected. The launch of the euro in January 1999 has become an unstoppable reality for everyone," Arthuis said.
He added the euro would be a "solid and credible" currency which would play a major role on the international scene.
Trichet echoed this, repeating that "the euro must be a solid, credible currency, at least as solid as the franc."
Commenting on the past rise in the dollar, Arthuis said, "I always said the dollar had room for appreciation. Let's not hide our satisfaction."
"It is excellent for French growth," he said.
